title: Check your understanding: Line Endings and Whitespace

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of line endings and whitespace?
options: Repository configuration should be understandable, portable and reviewed. Attributes and hooks can standardize workflows, but local hooks are not a substitute for server-side enforcement.
Git automatically backs up every file, including ignored and untracked files, to a remote.
The operation grants every contributor write access to the hosted repository.
questions.answer_key: Repository configuration should be understandable, portable and reviewed. Attributes and hooks can standardize workflows, but local hooks are not a substitute for server-side enforcement.
questions.explanation: Repository configuration should be understandable, portable and reviewed. Attributes and hooks can standardize workflows, but local hooks are not a substitute for server-side enforcement.

questions.prompt: Which command is the most direct starting point for this lesson’s example?
questions.explanation: Use `git check-attr -a -- path/to/file.txt` as the first inspection/action in the example, and then verify the result with the companion checks in the lesson.

questions.prompt: Which is the safest general practice when working with line endings and whitespace?
options: Inspect the repository state, verify the expected result, and protect valuable work before destructive or history-changing operations.
Run the most destructive option first; the reflog guarantees every file can always be recovered.
Assume the local command also changed the remote and satisfied all hosting-platform policies.
questions.answer_key: Inspect the repository state, verify the expected result, and protect valuable work before destructive or history-changing operations.
questions.explanation: Inspect the repository state, verify the expected result, and protect valuable work before destructive or history-changing operations.
